meta.principle: Round 1 heroes illustrated one sentence. Round 2 formats encode the EXPRESSION ITSELF — its spatial logic, its polysemy, its morphology, its iconic core — because the user's failure is un-mastered expressions, not forgotten sentences.

exemplars.format: Inside/Outside contrast — the idiom's spatial logic
exemplars.targets: form→meaning: makes the preposition itself the picture. Bonus: teaches the opposite (estar por fora) in the same glance.
exemplars.prompt: A single wide editorial illustration, contemporary flat style with rich warm/cool contrast. A huge transparent glass circle dominates the composition. INSIDE the circle: warm amber light, three people leaning in close sharing a secret over documents, relaxed and knowing; a small elegant label inside reads: por dentro. OUTSIDE the circle: cool blue dusk, one person standing alone straining to hear, hands cupped to the glass; a small label near them reads: por fora. At the bottom, one clean caption line: estar por dentro = estar informado. Only these three pieces of text, nothing else.

exemplars.format: Polysemy map — one word, three doors
exemplars.targets: confusability: tirado has three everyday readings; failing the card may be door-confusion, not vocabulary absence. One image holds all three so the brain files them as siblings. DESIGN RULE (user feedback): every door must be TAUGHT, not just labeled — gloss + micro-example under the image.

senses.label: en el suelo
senses.example: Tu abrigo está tirado en el suelo. — Your coat is lying on the floor.

senses.label: baratísimo
senses.example: ¿Solo un euro? ¡Está tirado! — Only one euro? That's a steal!

senses.label: facilísimo
senses.gloss: dead easy, a piece of cake
senses.example: El examen estaba tirado. — The exam was a piece of cake.

exemplars.prompt: One wide image divided into three equal arched doorways, museum-poster flat style, warm palette. Above all three arches, one large elegant banner reads: ESTÁ TIRADO. Through the LEFT arch: a wool coat crumpled on a wooden floor of a tidy room; small label below: en el suelo. Through the MIDDLE arch: a street-market stall with a huge slashed price tag showing 1€; small label below: baratísimo. Through the RIGHT arch: a person lounging in an armchair finishing a crossword with one pen stroke, feet up; small label below: facilísimo. Only these text elements: the banner and the three small labels.

exemplars.format: Morphology anatomy — the word as an exploded machine
exemplars.targets: meaning→form production: the failed direction is producing the subjunctive -e. The word itself becomes the object: BLOQUE as concrete blocks, des- as the chisel, the final -e as the pending golden switch.
exemplars.prompt: A technical-poster style illustration, annotated diagram aesthetic on deep slate background. The Spanish word 'se desbloquee' rendered huge as physical 3D letterforms in the center: the letters of BLOQUE are built from grey concrete blocks, cracking apart with dust; the prefix letters 'des' form a steel chisel prying the first block loose; the final letter 'e' is separate, glowing warm gold, hovering above a closed gate. A thin annotation line points to the golden e with the small label: todavía no. One caption line at the bottom: una vez que se desbloquee… The only text: the central word, the label todavía no, and the caption.

exemplars.format: Iconic poster — the metaphor's source domain as one emblem
exemplars.targets: what the video tried and failed at: one still, iconic composition beats six seconds of footage. Flat poster language, instantly re-recognizable at review time.
exemplars.prompt: A minimalist mid-century sports poster, flat vector style, only four colors: cream, deep green pitch, warm red, charcoal. Seen from high above: a football stadium bowl whose outer wall is shaped like the outline of a HOUSE with a pitched roof. Inside, the glowing green pitch; one tiny bright red player stands confidently at the center circle while a cluster of tiny grey opposing players huddles near a corner, small and out of place. Bold poster lettering at the bottom: GIOCARE IN CASA. No other text.

exemplars.format: Idiom glyphs — a permanent logo per expression
exemplars.targets: the escalation system: each rescued idiom gets ONE fixed pictographic stamp that then reappears on every future card of that idiom (new sentences, new exercises) — the constant identity across changing content.
exemplars.prompt: A sticker sheet of three bold circular glyphs on a neutral light background, evenly spaced in a row, app-icon style, thick outlines, two colors per glyph, no gradients, no text anywhere. Glyph 1: a flashlight projecting a bright amber cone of light onto an obstacle, with a sharp dark cone of shadow stretching behind it. Glyph 2: a circle with three dots snug INSIDE it and one lone dot excluded outside the rim. Glyph 3: an empty coat lying crumpled flat on the ground, viewed from above, one sleeve flung out. Clean, minimal, instantly readable at small size.

ladder.principle: A repeat failure is evidence that the CURRENT encoding didn't bind — so never regenerate a harder version of the same association; switch the encoding axis. One thing stays constant: the idiom's glyph, stamped on every card so all encounters accrue to one identity.
ladder.diagnosis: The revlog grain says WHICH direction fails: e2t card failing = production problem (meaning→form); t2e = recognition; cloze failing on grammar = form problem (agreement/subjunctive); fails clustered on one sense = polysemy confusion. The follow-up format is chosen by failure type, not rotated blindly.

strikes.trigger: idiom enters the struggle list (≥3 Agains/14d)
strikes.response: Rescue card v1: comic (scene encoding) + anchor + 3 fresh personalized sentences + cloze/production exercises. Glyph is minted and stamped.

strikes.trigger: still failing 7+ days after rescue v1 delivered
strikes.response: Switch axis, by diagnosis: production failure → morphology anatomy + production-heavy exercises; recognition failure → inside/outside-style contrast or iconic poster; polysemy confusion → polysemy map. ALL sentences replaced with new ones (never let the card be memorized instead of the idiom).

Personal-max: keyword mnemonic built on the user's other languages (ru/en/…), plus a metacognitive card that names the confusion explicitly ('you keep reading X as Y — here is the fork'), plus the idiom seeded into the next grammar/exercises2 wave so it recurs in other decks' contexts.

strikes.trigger: Again-rate of the parent idiom drops below threshold for 21 days
strikes.response: Rescue cards auto-retire (deck stays lean); glyph stays in the archive for any future relapse.
